title: Customer-specific Terraform customization patterns: overlays, variables, and module composition
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a set of supported Terraform customization patterns customers can use when deploying Redwood Private (VPC) so we can safely support customer-specific overlays without fragmenting ops or causing upgrade drift. The goal is to create opinionated, battle-tested patterns for: 1) overlay files vs. module inputs, 2) composition of higher-level modules (networking, nodes, control plane), 3) provider and backend scoping per-customer, and 4) minimal, supported extension points for bespoke needs (userData, additional security groups, cloud-init hooks). This ticket covers design, reference examples, automation (validation / plan checks), and a small migration guide for early customers that already have ad-hoc overrides.
background: We frequently see customers applying customizations in three places: patching generated TF (manual edits), shimming modules with local modules inside their repository, or using an external overlay/patching tool. These approaches cause problems during platform upgrades and make it hard for Redwood to reason about drift. Existing docs are fragmented; there is no single, recommended pattern that balances safety and flexibility. This work was requested by Solutions and Onboarding after incidents where upgrades failed due to unsupported customer changes in the managed modules.
proposed_solution: Ship a reference pattern library with: 1) a small core 'redwood_private' set of modules exposing stable input surfaces, 2) a documented overlay strategy using a 'customer' top-level module that composes core modules and injects allowed customizations, 3) variable profiles (customer_vars.tfvars) and provider aliasing guidance for multi-account deployments, 4) a validation CI job that runs 'terraform plan' against the composed configuration and flags unsupported changes, and 5) example repository templates (GCP/AWS) demonstrating per-customer backends, remote state workspace naming, and health-check modules. Include a set of supported extension points (hooks) that are versioned and checked during upgrades.
design_decisions: - Favor composition over forking: customers should compose 'redwood_private' rather than editing vendor modules.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Create reference examples and CI validator. Phase 2: Offer migration help to three pilot customers; run their existing configs through a compatibility scanner and propose minimal refactors. Phase 3: Integrate validation into onboarding pipeline and add detection to upgrade automation. Pilot target window: 3 weeks per customer. Migration scripts will be provided as a set of small Terraform re-org templates plus a helper script that rewrites backend configs and moves state with 'terraform state mv' guidance.
upgrade_and_rollback:
- Upgrades: We will maintain a 'compatibility matrix' for module inputs. During platform upgrades the upgrade runner will run the validator; if unsupported overlays are detected, it will: a) alert the customer and b) place the upgrade in a 'manual review' state. For minor input-only changes we will provide automated mapping transforms.
- Rollback: Keep a snapshot of remote state and module versions before the upgrade. If validation fails post-upgrade, run rollback automation to restore previous module version and state snapshot. Document manual rollback steps for edge cases.
health_checks_and_monitoring: Include a health-check module that creates: 1) a synthetic 'api-probe' (lambda/container) that hits the private control plane via peered connectors, 2) alerting rules for failed probes, 3) an SLO dashboard for provisioning/upgrade health. The Terraform pattern should expose hooks for customers to opt in/out and to customize probe intervals. Validation will include ensuring health-check resources exist for any new customer environment.
acceptance_criteria: Reference pattern docs published in the Private Deployments Confluence space with at least two cloud-specific examples (AWS, GCP)
Three example repos added to templates/private/ (aws-tenant, gcp-tenant, multi-account) demonstrating overlay and provider alias patterns
A CI validator that runs 'terraform init && terraform plan' and rejects configs that modify protected module files is merged to infra-ci
Migration guide and helper scripts uploaded to our onboarding repo with a worked example migrating one pilot customer
Health-check Terraform module included in the module registry and referenced in examples
tasks: Draft RFC describing supported customization surface and extension points
Implement 'redwood_private' stable module inputs and document deprecation policy
Create customer overlay example repositories (aws, gcp, multi-account)
Build CI validator (GH Action) to run terraform plan and compare diffs against allowed changes
Write migration scripts and run with pilot customers
Add health-check module and wire alerts/dashboards
Update onboarding playbook and solutions engineering runbook
risks: Customers may resist refactoring existing ad-hoc overrides and prefer immediate expedients
Edge-case customizations may not be representable by allowed hooks, leading to one-off escalations
Validator false positives could slow onboarding if too strict
State migration is risky; bad mapping could corrupt remote state if scripts are misused
mitigations: Provide automated codemods and a dry-run mode for migration scripts
Offer Solutions Eng time for first three migrations as part of pilot
Keep validator conservative initially and iterate rules based on pilot feedback
Require manual approvals and backups before any state-moving operation in migration helpers
open_questions: Should we officially support Terragrunt as an overlay pattern or only recommend vanilla Terraform composition?
How strict should the validator be by default for existing customers vs new customers?
What is the exact set of 'protected' module files we will prevent customers from modifying? (module internals vs api surface)
Do we want a lightweight SDK to generate customer overlay scaffolds or keep it as plain examples?
